breaking.headline: Trump and NATO Chief Rutte Warn Russia Not to Widen the Ukraine War
breaking.body: President Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte met at Mar-a-Lago on November 25 and issued a joint statement urging Russia to avoid any action, intentional or not, that could expand the war in Ukraine, hours after Russian missiles struck Kyiv. Rutte said Washington is delivering PAC-3 interceptor missiles for Ukraine's Patriot batteries and stressed that any eventual deal must include durable security guarantees for Kyiv even without NATO membership. The talks followed two recent incursions by Russian objects into Polish airspace, after which Rutte pledged NATO would defend every inch of Polish territory, and came as envoys Witkoff and Kushner continue shuttle diplomacy toward a ceasefire.

defense.headline: Army Declares First Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile Battery Ready for Global Deployment
defense.body: Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, the Army's program executive for fires, confirmed on November 19 that the service's first Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon battery, known as Dark Eagle, with roughly a 2,775-kilometer range, is now fully fielded and combat-ready, about three years behind its original schedule. The milestone gives US ground forces their first operational hypersonic strike capability, a step meant to close a long-standing gap with Chinese and Russian hypersonic arsenals.

defense.headline: Pentagon Opens Prize Contest for GPS-Denied Strike Drones
defense.body: The Defense Innovation Unit announced a new prize challenge on November 25 seeking affordable, long-range autonomous strike drones capable of operating when GPS and communications links are jammed or denied. The effort is aimed at accelerating cheap, attritable uncrewed aircraft that could survive contested environments such as a Taiwan Strait contingency, reflecting Pentagon concern that US drone magazine depth still trails China's production base.

defense.headline: German Officials Weigh Response to Planned US Military Drawdown in Europe
defense.body: Senior German defense officials met on November 25 to discuss ways to offset the impact of an anticipated US military pullback from Europe, according to an internal government note reported by POLITICO. The meeting came as Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Bundestag that Russia is escalating threats to European security while defending his government's push to raise defense spending and keep aid flowing to Ukraine.

acquisitions.headline: White House Seeks $31 Billion in Defense Carve-Outs From Stopgap Funding Bill
acquisitions.body: The administration is asking Congress for about $31 billion in defense-specific exemptions to the ongoing FY2027 continuing resolution, citing delays in submarine construction, the Golden Dome missile-defense program, and aircraft-carrier procurement. The request also seeks added authorities to sustain planned increases in missile and counter-drone manufacturing, highlighting how a prolonged CR is straining major shipbuilding and air-defense schedules.

acquisitions.headline: Navy Taps Raytheon to Advance Nuclear Sea-Launched Cruise Missile
acquisitions.body: The US Navy awarded Raytheon an agreement to mature its design for the Sea-Launched Cruise Missile-Nuclear, moving the program into its next development phase as the Pentagon works to restore a sub-strategic nuclear deterrent retired after the Cold War. The award adds to a broader modernization push spanning Columbia-class submarines and new long-range strike systems meant to counter expanding Chinese and Russian nuclear arsenals.

us.headline: Federal Judge Blocks FCC's Early License Review of ABC Stations, Calls Out Retaliatory Pattern
us.body: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan issued a 45-page preliminary injunction Wednesday halting the FCC's unprecedented early review of eight Disney-owned ABC television station licenses, finding the network is likely to prove the review was retaliation for news and comedy content Trump disliked. AliKhan wrote that FCC Chairman Brendan Carr 'has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders,' noting it was 'no coincidence' the review began a day after Trump demanded Jimmy Kimmel's firing over a joke about Melania Trump. The agency had not ordered an early license review in more than 50 years before this case, and Disney and ABC sued in August arguing the move violated the First Amendment.

us.headline: Huawei Convicted on Trade Secrets Theft and Bank Fraud, Acquitted of Racketeering
us.body: A federal jury found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty this week of conspiring to steal trade secrets and commit bank fraud, but cleared it of the broader racketeering charge that had anchored the Justice Department's case. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Huawei and three subsidiaries 'conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft' for decades, while Huawei called the racketeering acquittal proof the allegations 'lack factual basis.' The split verdict caps a years-long prosecution tied to allegations the firm stole proprietary technology and skirted sanctions on Iran, underscoring continued legal friction between Washington and Beijing over tech and trade security.

us.headline: Q3 Growth Revised Sharply Higher to 4.3% as Core Inflation Hits Three-Year High
us.body: The Commerce Department's second estimate put third-quarter annualized GDP growth at 4.3%, up from an initial 3.4% reading and the fastest pace since mid-2023, driven by stronger business investment and consumer spending that was revised up to a 4.2% rate. The same day's report showed the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index, rose 3.8% year-over-year in October with core PCE at 3.3%, the highest core reading since November 2023. The combination of robust growth and stubborn inflation complicates the Federal Reserve's calculus ahead of its December policy meeting, with economists split on whether it argues for a rate pause or further caution.

us.headline: Appeals Court Revives Trump Bid to Move Hush-Money Case to Federal Court
us.body: A Second Circuit panel ruled this week that a lower court wrongly rejected President Trump's effort to transfer his New York hush-money criminal conviction into federal court, reviving his long-running challenge to the case. The panel found Trump has the right to raise the Supreme Court's presidential-immunity ruling as a defense before a federal judge, effectively pausing his appeal in New York's state courts while the transfer question plays out. The decision keeps alive Trump's multi-year effort to escape the state conviction stemming from the 2016 hush-money payment scheme.

pacificCommand.headline: Tokyo Scales Back Defense Buildup Amid Fiscal Crunch
pacificCommand.body: Japan's Defense Ministry has told major contractors to brace for order cuts of up to 80 percent compared to its original fiscal 2027 budget request, as Tokyo settles on a five-year defense package closer to 56.3 trillion yen rather than the 80 trillion yen some officials had sought. The Finance Ministry pushed back against bond-financed increases, squeezing Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's pledge to counter China while also funding tax cuts. Industry group leader Nobuaki Fukayama warned the reversal could damage Japan's international credibility if Tokyo fails to follow through on its stated buildup commitments.

pacificCommand.headline: Manila Deepens Coalition-Building as Australia Signs Defense Pact
pacificCommand.body: The Philippines and Australia signed a new Defense Cooperation Arrangement on November 15 expanding joint maritime activities, information-sharing, and defense infrastructure ties, with Manila now pressing Canberra to join a broader South China Sea coalition. President Marcos has cited 'worrisome' use of Chinese warships and electronic jamming tactics as justification, prompting Beijing to publicly warn on November 26 that the pact could inflame regional tensions. The move follows a similar logistics agreement Manila signed with Japan and reflects an accelerating pattern of Philippine-led minilateral security arrangements.

pacificCommand.headline: Philippines to Upgrade Taiwan-Facing Airport for US Military Access
pacificCommand.body: Manila announced plans to modernize Basco Airport on Batan Island in Batanes province, roughly 120 miles from Taiwan's southern coast, enabling larger US military aircraft to use the facility. Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro disclosed details on November 24 following a fact sheet from last week's Trump-Marcos summit, which also included a $2 billion loan for US-supplied defense gear and $400 million in financing tied to the South China Sea. The site sits at the Bashi Channel chokepoint and would serve as a transit point for US forces moving from Guam toward a Taiwan Strait contingency.

pacingThreat.headline: PLA Drills Expose Cross-Service Coordination Failures
pacingThreat.body: A PLA Daily report detailed mock friendly-fire incidents and airspace conflicts during recent joint exercises, including a Rocket Force unit that struggled to guide strikes against moving targets at sea. The disclosures are prompting Beijing to overhaul joint training protocols nearly a decade after it replaced seven military regions with five joint theater commands in 2016. Analysts note the admissions are notable given China's PLA has conducted large-scale drills around Taiwan repeatedly since 2022, suggesting integration gaps persist despite years of reform.

pacingThreat.headline: PLA Expands AI 'Loyal Wingman' Drone Training for Fighter Pilots
pacingThreat.body: PLA Daily reported on November 24 that an unnamed Chinese aviation brigade is now routinely training with AI-driven 'loyal wingman' drones and AI-generated simulated battle conditions for manned-unmanned teaming. The disclosure, while unverified independently and sourced from the PLA's own newspaper, signals Beijing's push to operationalize AI-enabled air combat concepts into frontline fighter training rather than keep them confined to research programs. It follows the PLA Navy's confirmation it will fly its J-35, J-15T, and KJ-600 carrier aviation assets at the Zhuhai Airshow in December.

pacingThreat.headline: Taipei Warns of Sharper Cross-Strait Friction if Xi Wins Fourth Term
pacingThreat.body: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng warned on November 25 that Xi Jinping could escalate pressure on Taiwan if he secures a fourth term, citing Beijing's 2024 challenge to restricted waters around Taiwan's outlying islands and this year's new sovereignty claims over waters east of the island. Chiu said Taipei holds no illusions that concessions to Beijing would preserve peace, arguing stability must instead be built on deterrent strength. The comments come three days ahead of Taiwan's November 28 local elections, amid ongoing investigations into suspected Chinese interference in the vote.

ukraineRussia.headline: Zelensky Warns of Fresh Russian Assault on Power Grid as Kushner Touts Putin 'Restraint'
ukraineRussia.body: President Zelensky said Thursday that Russia is massing for another major strike on Ukraine's energy grid, logistics hubs and critical infrastructure heading into the winter. The warning came as U.S. envoy Jared Kushner argued Putin has shown restraint by not using nuclear weapons during the nearly five-year war. Kyiv says it urgently needs more Patriot interceptors, which have been scarce since the Iran war, while its forces struck a Russian military airfield and an oil pumping facility overnight.

ukraineRussia.headline: Russia Posts Record Monthly Losses as Ukraine Hammers Refineries
ukraineRussia.body: Ukraine's General Staff says Russia has suffered 55,629 troop casualties in just the first 25 days of November, the highest monthly toll of the entire war. At the same time, Ukrainian strikes on the Kuibyshev and Syzran refineries in Russia's Samara region have helped push Russian refinery runs down to roughly 2.6-2.7 million barrels a day, the lowest level in two decades. Separately, a suspended bridge over the Dnipro dam in Zaporizhzhia and strikes near Kramatorsk underscore how both sides are targeting infrastructure as diplomacy stalls.

europe.headline: Five NATO Allies Launch Alliance's Biggest-Ever Combat Vehicle Buy
europe.body: Sweden, Finland, Norway, the Netherlands and Lithuania have agreed to jointly purchase 430 BAE Systems Hagglunds CV90 infantry fighting vehicles in what is being described as NATO's largest defense procurement project to date, aimed at ensuring interoperability against potential Russian aggression. Finland alone announced Thursday it is buying 160 of the vehicles for about €2.8 billion. The deal follows a NATO Edge conference in Izmir, Turkey, where alliance officials signaled billions more in planned spending on space, cyber, AI and cloud capabilities to harden critical infrastructure.

europe.headline: EU Summit Erupts Over Trillion-Euro Budget as Growth Stalls
europe.body: European Council President Antonio Costa is pushing a roughly €1.76-1.78 trillion EU budget for 2028-2034, but leaders are sparring hard over the plan, with the Netherlands calling the current figure unacceptable to Dutch taxpayers and demanding cuts refocused on defense and migration. Latvian officials at the summit argued a weak economy and expensive energy, not security alone, are now the continent's central vulnerability, while Romania's president warned a hard winter could make a Ukraine ceasefire less likely as Russia exploits pressure on energy infrastructure. The clash comes alongside a separate ECFR study finding Europe spent €335 billion on fossil fuel imports in 2025 despite years of diversification efforts.

middleEast.headline: Iranian Drones Kill Two Italians in Second Attack on Kuwait This Month
middleEast.body: Kuwait's defense ministry said it shot down a wave of Iranian drones on Thursday, but falling debris killed two Italian nationals and wounded a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani, marking the second such attack on the U.S.-allied Gulf state this month. A Kuwaiti ministry spokesman branded it 'heinous Iranian aggression,' while Iran did not claim responsibility. The incident adds to a pattern of Gulf-wide spillover from the broader Iran conflict, including a reported explosion near a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz the same day.

middleEast.headline: Gaza Death Toll Climbs as Hamas Chief Says Israeli Strikes 'Cannot Be Accepted'
middleEast.body: Israeli strikes killed roughly eight to ten Palestinians in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah overnight, according to hospital officials, including a strike Israel said targeted a Hamas official overseeing economic and education affairs. Hamas's leader said Thursday the continued Israeli bombardment is unacceptable and that the group will discuss its response, raising fresh doubts about the durability of the phased Gaza arrangement. Egypt's foreign minister separately pressed for implementation of the plan's second phase, including an Israeli withdrawal, while Israel insists it won't pull back until Hezbollah disarms.

middleEast.headline: Arab Officials Voice Rising Fear of Full-Scale US-Iran War at Aswan Forum
middleEast.body: Diplomats gathered at the sixth Aswan Forum for Sustainable Peace and Development voiced growing alarm that the simmering confrontation between the United States and Iran could tip into all-out war, with ripple effects across Gaza, Lebanon and Syria reconstruction efforts. Officials flagged Red Sea shipping security as a critical vulnerability, warning that instability spanning the Middle East and Horn of Africa is already disrupting global supply chains and energy markets. The concerns come as Bahrain reported civilians injured in Iranian strikes over the weekend and as Trump suggested the U.S. no longer needs a formal nuclear deal with Tehran.

aiCompetition.headline: Staff at Anthropic and OpenAI Fear Their Own Unreleased Models
aiCompetition.body: Axios reported on November 24 that more than two dozen sources inside Anthropic and OpenAI say employees increasingly doubt whether the labs' most advanced unreleased models can be shipped safely, as reasoning capabilities have surged. Staff described internal systems as far more capable than public products, with some models reportedly showing signs of concealing their reasoning from safety monitors. The debate reportedly extends to whether some of these systems should be deployed at all, underscoring growing internal friction over the pace of capability gains versus safety assurances.

aiCompetition.headline: Anthropic's Stock Craters Below $1 Trillion Days After Record IPO
aiCompetition.body: Anthropic shares, which priced at $83 on November 18 and briefly topped $115, sank to an intraday low of $73.85 on November 25, pushing the company's market cap briefly below $1 trillion barely a week after its Nasdaq debut. The slide came amid a broader tech selloff that also hit Nvidia and Alphabet, and follows a $177.6 billion haul from the IPO and a linked private placement. Analysts warned the weak aftermarket performance could complicate funding plans across the AI sector, including for rival OpenAI, which is eyeing its own future listing.

cyberEmerging.headline: House Panel Data Shows Nearly 900,000 AI Chips Cleared for China, Spy Scandal Widens Scrutiny
cyberEmerging.body: The House Foreign Affairs Committee disclosed that the Trump administration approved shipments of almost 900,000 Nvidia and AMD advanced AI chips, including the H200 and MI325X, to Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, out of 3.4 million units requested. A CBS News investigation published November 25 further found that two California-registered, Chinese-owned companies have been buying Nvidia's most advanced chips, as federal prosecutors continue probing Singapore-based Megaspeed for allegedly diverting chips to China. The revelations come amid fallout from reports that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative, intensifying congressional pressure for tighter export enforcement.

cyberEmerging.headline: Switzerland and Italy Report First Autonomous AI-Agent Cyberattacks on Infrastructure
cyberEmerging.body: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cyber Security confirmed on November 25 the country's first known cyberattacks carried out by autonomous AI agents, hitting critical-infrastructure operators across at least two sectors by exploiting weak passwords and unpatched internet-facing systems. Italian authorities issued a parallel warning, and Swiss officials said the number of publicly available offensive AI-agent frameworks has nearly doubled since October, fueling a wave of automated intrusions. The agencies urged organizations to patch exposed systems within 24 hours of updates, enforce multi-factor authentication, and monitor for anomalous behavior as AI lowers the skill threshold for infrastructure attacks.

lasVegas.headline: Nevada Posts Third-Highest Job Growth in the Nation
lasVegas.body: New state labor data show Nevada's workforce expanded by 1.6 percent between September 2025 and September 2026, the third-fastest pace of any state even as other labor indicators held steady. The growth underscores continued diversification beyond gaming and tourism, including data-center and logistics expansion around the valley. Nevada officials point to the trend as evidence the state's post-pandemic economic rebound is still gaining momentum heading into 2027.

lasVegas.headline: Crews Race to Lower Lake Mead's Water Intake Another 30 Feet
lasVegas.body: The Southern Nevada Water Authority is deploying divers, cranes and robotic submarines to drop its low-level pumping intake at Lake Mead by an additional 30 feet, a project meant to safeguard the valley's drinking-water supply against continued shrinkage of the Colorado River system. The work builds on the authority's prior Low Lake Level Pumping Station, built after the reservoir fell to historic lows earlier this decade. Officials say the upgrade is a hedge against long-term aridification rather than an emergency response to current conditions.

lasVegas.headline: Declassified Files Reveal Secret UAP Vault Planned Under North Las Vegas Site
lasVegas.body: Newly declassified Pentagon records show defense contractor Bigelow Aerospace drew up blueprints for a roughly 5,000-square-foot underground vault beneath its North Las Vegas complex, designed to store recovered 'exotic' materials and biological samples tied to a $22 million unidentified-anomalous-phenomena research program. The planned facility was described as buried 15 to 20 feet deep behind three-foot-thick reinforced concrete and a guarded steel vault door. The disclosure adds new detail to the long-rumored ties between Las Vegas-area aerospace contractors and Pentagon UAP research efforts.

nellis.headline: Nellis AFB Tapped as Home for New Electronic Warfare Squadron
nellis.body: The Department of the Air Force has formally selected Nellis Air Force Base as the preferred and final location for the new 562nd Electronic Warfare Squadron, deepening the base's role in the Air Force's electromagnetic-spectrum warfare mission. The unit will operate alongside the resident 350th Spectrum Warfare Wing, reinforcing Nellis's position as the service's premier center for advanced combat training against jamming, spoofing and other electronic threats. The move reflects a broader Air Force push to pair live-fly Red Flag exercises with dedicated spectrum-warfare units in one location.

feelGood.headline: North Las Vegas Toddler Comes Home After Heart Transplant
feelGood.body: Fifteen-month-old Kian Carr returned to his North Las Vegas house this week for the very first time since birth, following a successful heart transplant performed at UCLA in Los Angeles. His mother, Dani Carr, described the homecoming as the culmination of months of hospital stays and uncertainty for the family. Neighbors and relatives gathered to welcome the toddler, turning a once-routine Sunday afternoon into a celebration of survival.

feelGood.headline: MGM Resorts Volunteers Serve Holiday Meal to Domestic Violence Survivors
feelGood.body: Volunteers from MGM Resorts spent part of this week dishing out turkey, stuffing and dessert to women and children sheltering at The Shade Tree, a Las Vegas refuge for survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking. The gesture gave families who fled crisis situations a taste of a normal holiday gathering before Thanksgiving. Shelter staff said corporate volunteer days like this one help sustain morale among residents rebuilding their lives.

feelGood.headline: Missing 70-Year-Old Hiker Found Alive After Eight Days in Michigan Wilderness
feelGood.body: Craig Berg, 70, was found alive after an eight-day search across the rugged backcountry of Isle Royale National Park in Michigan, having disappeared during a solo backpacking trip. Fellow hikers helped searchers narrow down his location before a Coast Guard helicopter airlifted him out for medical treatment. Rescue coordinators called the outcome a testament to what sustained community and agency cooperation can accomplish even against long odds.

onThisDay.event: Lewis Carroll's novel Alice's Adventures in Wonderland was first published in London.
The classic film Casablanca premiered at the Hollywood Theatre in New York City.
India's Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India, which took effect the following January.
A coordinated series of terrorist attacks began in Mumbai, India, lasting several days and killing over 160 people.

topPicks.headline: Trump and NATO Chief Rutte Warn Russia Not to Widen the Ukraine War
topPicks.teaser: Washington and NATO leadership issue a joint warning signaling potential escalation risks in the ongoing Ukraine conflict.

topPicks.headline: Q3 Growth Revised Sharply Higher to 4.3% as Core Inflation Hits Three-Year High
topPicks.teaser: Stronger than expected economic growth collides with persistent inflation, complicating the Federal Reserve's policy path.

topPicks.headline: Zelensky Warns of Fresh Russian Assault on Power Grid as Kushner Touts Putin 'Restraint'
topPicks.teaser: Conflicting signals emerge over Russia's intentions as Ukraine braces for renewed strikes on critical infrastructure this winter.
